The invention provides a sensor-guided, automated system that is capable of intelligently cutting crustaceans, such as crab and lobster, into a plurality of portions, as directed. More particularly, the present system is capable of effectively butchering each individual crustacean in response to how the system's sensor(s) assess the physical characteristics of each crustacean as it arrives via a conveyor belt. The system generally comprises: an intake apparatus for receiving a crustacean; a sensor-guided positioning (“SGP”) system for determining the presence, location, orientation and size of the crustacean on the intake apparatus, coupling the crustacean, and placing the crustacean into a holding system for butchering; a holding system for retaining the crustacean in an optimal fixed position for butchering; a sensor-guided butchering (“SGB”) system for determining the locations on a crustacean body to be cut based on the desired output of crustacean portions, and cutting the crustacean at the chosen locations to produce optimal crustacean products; and an outlet apparatus which discharges the butchered crustacean from the system for subsequent packaging.

The invention describes an automated, sensor-controlled system designed to cut crustaceans, including crabs and lobsters, into multiple designated sections. Specifically, the system can process each crustacean individually by adjusting its butchering operation according to the physical features detected by one or more sensors as the crustacean is delivered on a conveyor belt.

In general, the system includes an intake mechanism that receives the crustacean; a sensor-guided positioning, or SGP, system that identifies whether the crustacean is present and determines its position, orientation, and size on the intake mechanism, then engages the crustacean and transfers it into a holding arrangement for cutting; a holding system that secures the crustacean in a fixed, optimized position for butchering; a sensor-guided butchering, or SGB, system that determines where the crustacean’s body should be cut according to the desired final portions and performs cuts at those selected points to create optimized crustacean products; and an outlet mechanism that removes the cut crustacean from the system so it can proceed to packaging.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a sensor-guided automated system for cutting crustaceans, such as crabs, lobsters, and similar shellfish, into multiple portions suitable for downstream handling, processing, and packaging. The system is designed to accommodate natural variations in the size, shape, orientation, and anatomical structure of individual crustaceans, thereby improving consistency, yield, and processing efficiency when compared with manual cutting or fixed-position automated cutters.

In operation, each crustacean is delivered to the system on a conveyor belt or other intake transport mechanism. As the crustacean arrives, the system evaluates its physical characteristics and uses that information to adjust the butchering process for that particular specimen. These characteristics may include the crustacean’s presence on the conveyor, its position, orientation, overall dimensions, body shape, leg or claw placement, and other relevant anatomical features. By assessing each crustacean individually, the system can determine how best to handle and cut the crustacean according to a desired portioning pattern.

The system generally includes an intake apparatus, a sensor-guided positioning system, a holding system, a sensor-guided butchering system, and an outlet apparatus. The intake apparatus receives crustaceans and conveys them toward the processing area. The sensor-guided positioning system monitors incoming crustaceans and determines their presence, location, orientation, and size before they are transferred into the holding system. Based on sensor data, the positioning system may align, rotate, center, or otherwise manipulate the crustacean so that it is properly situated for cutting.

Once positioned, the crustacean is secured by the holding system. The holding system maintains the crustacean in a stable orientation during the cutting operation, reducing movement and helping ensure accurate cuts. The holding system may be adjustable to accommodate crustaceans of different sizes and shapes, and it may cooperate with the sensor-guided positioning system to ensure that the crustacean is held in a predetermined or dynamically selected cutting position.

The sensor-guided butchering system then determines optimal cut locations based on the sensed physical characteristics of the crustacean and the desired output portions. For example, the system may calculate cut paths to divide a crab or lobster into halves, sections, claws, legs, body portions, or other marketable segments. The cutting mechanism is then actuated according to these calculated locations to portion the crustacean accurately and consistently.

After cutting, the resulting portions are transferred to the outlet apparatus for subsequent handling. The outlet apparatus may convey the cut portions to a packaging station, inspection station, sorting system, or additional processing equipment. In this manner, the invention provides an automated, adaptive butchering system capable of processing crustaceans with improved precision, reduced labor requirements, and greater consistency in the final packaged product.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to an automated system and method for processing crustaceans, such as crabs, lobsters, and similar shellfish, in a controlled and efficient manner. The system is designed to receive individual crustaceans on a conveyor or other transport mechanism and move them through a processing line where each item is evaluated and handled according to its own physical characteristics. Rather than relying on fixed cutting positions or manual labor, the invention uses sensors, imaging devices, or other detection equipment to determine whether a crustacean is present, where it is located on the conveyor, how it is oriented, and what its relevant dimensions are.

After the crustacean is detected and assessed, the system uses the gathered information to guide subsequent handling operations. A positioning mechanism may rotate, shift, align, or otherwise orient the crustacean so that it is placed in a proper processing position. Once correctly positioned, a holding or clamping arrangement secures the crustacean to prevent unwanted movement during cutting. Based on the detected size, shape, and orientation of the crustacean, a controller determines one or more cutting paths or cutting locations that correspond to the desired final product portions. These portions may include, for example, claws, legs, tails, body sections, or other marketable cuts, depending on the type of crustacean being processed and the intended packaging format.

The cutting operation may be performed by one or more blades, saws, water jets, or other cutting tools arranged to divide the crustacean accurately and repeatably. Because the system can adjust the cutting process for each individual crab or lobster, it can accommodate natural variation in size and shape while still producing consistent portion outputs. This reduces waste, improves yield, and provides more uniform product pieces for sorting, weighing, packaging, or further processing.

In operation, the conveyor feeds crustaceans into the sensing area, where the system identifies the presence and position of each item. The control system then calculates the necessary adjustments and commands the positioning, holding, and cutting components to act in sequence. Once the crustacean has been cut into the selected portions, the processed pieces may continue along the conveyor to downstream equipment, such as graders, inspection stations, packing machines, or freezing systems.

By combining automated conveyance, sensor-based assessment, adaptive positioning, secure holding, and controlled cutting, the invention provides a precise and individualized approach to crustacean butchering. It enables high-throughput processing while maintaining product consistency and optimizing the value of each crustacean. As a result, the system reduces manual handling, improves worker safety, increases processing efficiency, and produces optimized crustacean portions suitable for commercial packaging and distribution.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style summary for an automated sensor-guided machine that cuts crustaceans like crabs and lobsters into portions on a conveyor system.
counterfactuals.output:
An automated crustacean portioning machine is disclosed for processing crabs, lobsters, and similar shellfish into selected portions while transported along a conveyor system. The machine includes a conveyor configured to receive and advance individual crustaceans through a cutting station, one or more sensors arranged to detect position, orientation, size, anatomical landmarks, shell contours, or other physical characteristics of each crustacean, and a controller operatively coupled to the sensors and to one or more cutting mechanisms.

In operation, the sensors generate measurement data as a crustacean approaches or enters the cutting station. The controller processes the measurement data to determine a cutting plan, including one or more cut locations, cut angles, timing parameters, and/or blade trajectories corresponding to a desired portioning pattern. The cutting mechanism is then actuated in synchronism with conveyor movement to divide the crustacean into predetermined portions, such as claws, legs, body sections, tail sections, or other market-ready pieces.

The system may include adjustable guides, positioning members, hold-down devices, clamps, or alignment features to stabilize the crustacean during cutting. The cutting mechanism may comprise rotary blades, reciprocating blades, band saws, water jets, or other cutting tools mounted on fixed or movable actuators. The sensors may include optical cameras, depth sensors, laser scanners, ultrasonic sensors, weight sensors, proximity sensors, or combinations thereof. The controller may compensate for variations in species, size, orientation, and irregular shell geometry, thereby enabling automated cutting without requiring manual placement into dedicated fixtures.

In certain embodiments, the conveyor includes spaced carriers, trays, cleats, or pockets for locating crustaceans during transport. The machine may further include a user interface for selecting portioning programs, a memory storing species-specific cutting parameters, and feedback sensors for verifying cut completion or detecting misalignment. Processed portions may be discharged onto an output conveyor, while rejected or improperly positioned crustaceans may be diverted for reprocessing or manual inspection.

The disclosed machine improves throughput, consistency, labor efficiency, and operator safety in crustacean processing by automatically identifying each crustacean and controlling cutting operations based on sensed characteristics rather than fixed assumptions regarding size or orientation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a technical abstract describing an invention for intelligently butchering individual crustaceans using sensors, positioning mechanisms, holding fixtures, cutting systems, and discharge apparatus.
counterfactuals.output:
A system and method are disclosed for intelligently butchering individual crustaceans, such as crabs, lobsters, or similar shellfish, on an automated processing line. The system includes an infeed configured to receive a single crustacean, one or more holding fixtures adapted to restrain the crustacean in a selected orientation, and a sensing subsystem configured to determine anatomical, dimensional, positional, and/or species-specific characteristics of the crustacean. The sensing subsystem may include optical sensors, depth cameras, weight sensors, force sensors, X-ray or hyperspectral sensors, or combinations thereof, and may generate data identifying cutting locations, shell boundaries, joint positions, leg orientation, body centerline, or edible-meat regions.

A controller processes the sensor data to determine a customized butchering plan for the individual crustacean and actuates one or more positioning mechanisms to align the crustacean relative to a cutting system. The positioning mechanisms may include robotic arms, rotary indexers, linear actuators, clamping jaws, compliant supports, or adjustable nests. The cutting system may include knives, saws, waterjets, rotary blades, ultrasonic cutters, or shearing members selectively positioned and operated according to the butchering plan. The system may perform operations including splitting, sectioning, limb removal, claw separation, shell opening, gill removal, trimming, or portioning while reducing damage to edible tissue.

After cutting, a discharge apparatus transfers butchered portions, waste material, and/or separated components to designated outlets, conveyors, bins, or downstream processing stations. The controller may adapt cutting parameters based on detected crustacean size, orientation, shell hardness, species, or yield objectives, and may update operating settings using feedback from the sensing subsystem. The invention thereby enables automated, individualized crustacean processing with improved accuracy, throughput, yield, and consistency relative to fixed-path mechanical butchering systems.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an automated crustacean butchering apparatus comprising an intake conveyor, sensor-guided positioning system, holding system, sensor-guided cutting system, and outlet for packaging.
counterfactuals.output:
An automated crustacean butchering apparatus can comprise a coordinated processing line designed to receive, orient, secure, cut, and discharge crustaceans for downstream packaging.

The apparatus includes an **intake conveyor** configured to transport crustaceans, such as crabs, lobsters, or similar shellfish, from a loading area into a processing zone. The conveyor may include spaced flights, pockets, trays, or alignment guides to maintain separation between individual crustaceans and provide predictable presentation to downstream components.

A **sensor-guided positioning system** is arranged along or adjacent to the intake conveyor. This system may include optical cameras, depth sensors, laser scanners, weight sensors, or machine-vision equipment configured to detect the location, orientation, size, and anatomical features of each crustacean. Based on sensor data, a controller determines the position of the body, shell, legs, claws, tail, or other relevant structures and actuates positioning elements such as robotic grippers, guide rails, rotary platforms, pushers, or indexing trays to orient the crustacean in a desired butchering position.

A **holding system** is provided at a cutting station to secure the crustacean during processing. The holding system may include clamps, compliant pads, vacuum fixtures, articulated grippers, hinged retainers, or shaped nests that engage the shell or appendages without excessive crushing. The holding system may be adjustable under control of the sensor-guided positioning system to accommodate variation in crustacean size and shape.

A **sensor-guided cutting system** is positioned relative to the holding system. The cutting system may include one or more powered blades, rotary cutters, reciprocating knives, waterjet cutters, saws, or robotic cutting tools. Sensors provide feedback regarding the precise anatomical location of the crustacean, allowing the controller to guide the cutting tool along predetermined cut paths, such as separating claws, legs, tail portions, carapace sections, or other edible parts. The cutting system may adjust cutting depth, angle, force, and trajectory in real time based on detected shell geometry and product specifications.

After cutting, processed portions are released onto an **outlet conveyor or chute** that transfers the butchered crustacean parts to a packaging area. The outlet may include sorting lanes, reject gates, weighing stations, inspection sensors, or buffers for integration with automated packaging equipment. A controller coordinates operation of the intake conveyor, positioning system, holding system, cutting system, and outlet to provide continuous or indexed automated processing of crustaceans with improved consistency, throughput, and reduced manual handling.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an invention summary in patent language for a robotic system that receives crustaceans, assesses their physical characteristics, positions and holds them, cuts them optimally, and outputs the processed pieces.
counterfactuals.output:
## Invention Summary

The present invention relates generally to automated food-processing equipment and, more particularly, to a robotic system and method for receiving, identifying, positioning, restraining, cutting, and discharging crustaceans or portions thereof in an optimized manner.

In one embodiment, the invention provides a robotic crustacean-processing system comprising an input station configured to receive one or more crustaceans, a sensing station configured to assess physical characteristics of each crustacean, a positioning and holding assembly configured to orient and secure the crustacean in a selected processing position, a cutting assembly configured to perform one or more cuts based at least in part on the assessed physical characteristics, and an output station configured to discharge processed crustacean pieces.

The sensing station may include one or more imaging devices, depth sensors, weight sensors, force sensors, hyperspectral sensors, X-ray sensors, ultrasonic sensors, or combinations thereof. The physical characteristics assessed by the sensing station may include, without limitation, size, length, width, height, weight, shell geometry, appendage position, claw location, tail position, body orientation, species, grade, shell hardness, meat distribution, defect condition, or anatomical landmark location.

A controller is operatively coupled to the sensing station, the positioning and holding assembly, and the cutting assembly. The controller may be configured to generate a digital model or processing profile of the crustacean and determine one or more optimal cutting paths. The optimal cutting paths may be selected to maximize meat recovery, produce standardized portions, avoid undesired shell fragments, reduce waste, preserve visual appearance, improve throughput, or satisfy a predetermined product specification.

The positioning and holding assembly may include one or more robotic manipulators, conveyors, clamps, vacuum holders, compliant grippers, articulated fingers, alignment guides, cradles, or restraining members. The assembly may be configured to rotate, translate, center, elevate, invert, spread, compress, or otherwise orient the crustacean relative to the cutting assembly. In certain embodiments, the holding assembly applies controlled force sufficient to restrain the crustacean while reducing crushing, deformation, or damage to edible portions.

The cutting assembly may include one or more blades, rotary cutters, reciprocating knives, band saws, waterjet cutters, ultrasonic cutters, laser cutters, shear mechanisms, or other cutting tools. The cutting assembly may be movable along one or more axes by a robotic arm, gantry, linear actuator, rotary actuator, or multi-axis motion platform. The controller may adjust cutting depth, angle, speed, force, tool selection, and trajectory according to the assessed characteristics of the individual crustacean.

In operation, a crustacean is received at the input station and transported to the sensing station. The sensing station acquires data corresponding to the physical characteristics of the crustacean. The controller processes the acquired data to identify anatomical landmarks and determine an optimized cutting plan. The positioning and holding assembly then orients and secures the crustacean in accordance with the cutting plan. The cutting assembly performs one or more controlled cuts to divide, open, section, split, trim, shell, or otherwise process the crustacean. Processed pieces are subsequently transferred to the output station for collection, sorting, packaging, inspection, or further processing.

In some embodiments, the system includes a feedback mechanism configured to monitor cutting performance or product quality. The feedback mechanism may include vision inspection, force monitoring, acoustic sensing, tool-position sensing, or post-cut measurement. The controller may modify subsequent cutting operations based on the feedback, thereby enabling adaptive processing of crustaceans having variable size, species, shape, or condition.

In further embodiments, the system may classify processed pieces and direct them to different discharge paths according to grade, size, weight, cut type, or quality. The output station may include conveyors, bins, sorters, diverters, robotic pick-and-place devices, or packaging interfaces.

Accordingly, the invention provides an automated robotic crustacean-processing system capable of individualized assessment, adaptive positioning, secure holding, optimized cutting, and controlled discharge of processed crustacean pieces, thereby improving consistency, yield, labor efficiency, sanitation, and throughput relative to manual or non-adaptive processing systems.
